nodes.label: Reconstruction Paradigm
nodes.rationale: The contest is reconstruction (restore the baseline original layout), not floorplan optimization. Because Cost=(1+0.5(HPWL_gap+Area_gap))*exp(2V_rel), only gap=0 AND V_rel=0 gives Cost=1.0; 'finding the best solution' always yields HPWL_gap>0 hence Cost>1. This is why unsupervised loss and per-block ML are structurally weak here.

nodes.label: Per-case Cost / Total Score Formula
nodes.rationale: Cost=(1+0.5(HPWL_gap+Area_gap))*exp(2*V_rel)*max(0.7,R^0.3); infeasible=10.0; feasible capped at 9.999999; Total Score = sum(Cost*e^(n/12))/sum(weight).

nodes.label: RuntimeFactor Lever (RF axis)
nodes.rationale: A new axis orthogonal to quality, opened once quality converged. Local eval forces RF=1.0 (hiding the official per-case max(0.7,(t/median)^0.3)). Since cost is proportional to t^0.3 and big cases are quality-locked, cutting big-case wall time is a median-independent real-score gain.

nodes.label: Baseline-free Portfolio Proxy
nodes.rationale: Runs ~40 deterministic profiles in parallel and selects the best via proxy=(area/A_hat + _RH*hpwl/hmin)*exp(2*vrel); since M13 the proxy is an oracle-ceiling perfect selector.

nodes.label: Proxy _RH=1.4 Lever
nodes.rationale: Proxy under-weights HPWL (hmin>hbase by ~1.3-1.4); _RH=1.4 compensates and hits the oracle ceiling; basin flat over [1.1,1.6] so it generalizes.

nodes.label: Shapely vrel Proxy Metric
nodes.rationale: vrel must be computed with shapely (not the C++ union-find METRICS) because a 1e-3 tolerance disagrees on 34/100 cases.

nodes.label: Free-aspect Six Sub-axes (M29-M37)
nodes.rationale: Six gated aspect-ratio sub-axes (single free, decoupled boundary, cluster uniform, per-member cluster, anchored, MIB) that drove 1.3843->1.3269; all off = bit-identical.

nodes.label: Boundary-aspect Dims (2.50/0.40)
nodes.rationale: LEFT/RIGHT-only aspect 2.50, TOP/BOTTOM-only 0.40 raises edge capacity to lower boundary violation; highest-ROI insight. Must be UNIFORM (per-block FREE_BOUNDARY is dead).

nodes.label: MIB Shape Unification (apply_safe_mib_dims)
nodes.rationale: Unify multi-instantiation-block shapes (master if compatible, else sqrt-avg square) preserving the 1% hard constraint; drove MIB violations 145->0.

nodes.label: Cluster Construction
nodes.rationale: Pure-movable clusters become composite items (3 orderings x 5 layouts, lexicographic key); mixed preplaced+movable clusters are anchored against the preplaced wall.

nodes.label: Fixed-frame Greedy Packing
nodes.rationale: Tries 4-5 outline frames (smaller area first), boundary-aware candidate scoring (bbox_area + anchor + wire*WIRE + BP_W*boundary_miss, ww base x2000); layout_score picks the best frame.

nodes.label: Compaction Area Lever
nodes.rationale: Post-pack boundary-preserving compaction attacks dead-space area_gap; candidate chosen by true-cost csc, NOT layout_score (which over-weights boundary).

nodes.label: HPWL Push Lever (M14-16/24)
nodes.rationale: Post-processing HPWL reduction: free-single slide, boundary free-axis slide, same-size swap, cross-obstacle jump; hgap is the dominant quality gap.

nodes.label: Pack-order Lever (M17-M27)
nodes.rationale: Order/placement layer closed; oracle-perm proves a perfect order gains only +0.005% so ordering/ML/LNS is permanently closed. Shipped GUIDE_MED.

nodes.label: Teammate 1.0322 Label-leak Oracle
nodes.rationale: Teammate's 1.0322 reads the local validation label (oracle); it falls back on the hidden test so is not applicable. Legit ceiling ~1.62; true ceiling 1.1079 (fp_sol verbatim).

nodes.label: Reconstruction RED-confirmed (M40)
nodes.rationale: Spectral recursive-bisection slicing fails both gates: X-from-connectivity (movable X-order Spearman 0.009) and deterministic Y-order (+159% vs oracle-Y). Netlist is generated independently of layout, so reconstruction is information-theoretically impossible without the label.

nodes.label: %.17g Output Precision Requirement
nodes.rationale: Geometry printed as %.17g not %.10f; rounding breaks exact abutments into spurious shapely cluster fragments (~144/100 cases, -6.3% single-base regression).

nodes.label: M41 Swap-profile Cut
nodes.rationale: First RF shot: drop the 6 ORDER_SWAP/ORDER_MOVE profiles (pure runtime dead weight); avg 9.89->5.90s, ~-12% projected real, local +0.06% fiction.

nodes.label: M42 Big-redundant Profile Cut
nodes.rationale: Drop the 21 build profiles winning no n>100 case (_BIG_REDUNDANT_IDX, block_count>100); quality bit-identical, avg 5.90->4.73s, big-case wall halved.

nodes.label: M45 Band Tiers + Cores-adaptive
nodes.rationale: Redundancy generalized to band-scoped under a strict selection-preserving gate (per-case cost equality). Tier-3 universal (-1.2~1.5%), tier-4 low-core (cores<=8, -9.3% @4c).

nodes.label: M46 Hot-path Exact Speedup
nodes.rationale: Exact opts A/B/C (skip unread xs/ys sets, hash dedup, 32x32 grid overlap) in constructive.cpp pack hot path; 4100/4100 positions bit-identical, avg 4.73->2.70s.

nodes.label: M47 Wrapper Overhead Fix
nodes.rationale: Serial shapely proxy was 29% of n>100 wall (never modeled); fix = as_completed overlap (one at a time; concurrent = GIL thrash 4x worse) + tolist proxy internals (x11.5, 300/300 bit-identical). avg 2.70->1.85s.

nodes.label: M48 Submission Hardening
nodes.rationale: Compiler chain (g++/clang++/c++ x -O3/-O2) + 1-block binary smoke (mtime shortcut would accept a foreign unrunnable exe), plus solve() 3-layer safety net (Exception->SA->row layout). Zero score change.

nodes.label: M49 Measured REFINE Band Cut
nodes.rationale: First measured quality trade: no exact REFINE cut exists (17/260 winners improve at the last pass), so ship REFINE_ITERS 12->4 for n>100 via _band_env; +0.027% local (1.3277->1.3281), band wall -50%, avg 1.85->1.54s.

nodes.label: _pool_indices() Four-stage Profile Filter
nodes.rationale: Wrapper index-based filter (ICCAD_ADAPTIVE_POOL=1 default) applying M41 swap cut, M42 big-redundant cut, M45 band-drop and low-core drops; =0 restores full 40-profile quality-best.

nodes.label: rf_score_model.py RF Projection Model
nodes.rationale: Offline (never-ship) RF-aware projection model: loads audit_cache.pkl, projects real Total over median M, regenerates drop constants with a strict selection-preserving gate.

nodes.label: constructive.cpp (Constructive Placer)
nodes.rationale: C++ constructive fixed-frame placer (B-route rewrite); deterministic, contains M9-M37 behavior plus M46 hot-path exact speedups and METRICS stderr.

nodes.label: optimizer_constructive.py (Portfolio Wrapper)
nodes.rationale: 40-profile portfolio wrapper with shapely proxy (_RH=1.4), _pool_indices() four-stage cuts, M47 overlapped proxy, M48 safety nets, and M49 _band_env REFINE overlay.

nodes.label: FloorSet Dataset
nodes.rationale: A VLSI floorplanning dataset of 2M synthetic fixed-outline layouts (PyTorch tensors) with real-world SoC constraints; basis for ICCAD 2026 Contest Problem C.

nodes.label: FloorSet-Prime
nodes.rationale: 1M-layout sub-dataset allowing polygonal (non-rectangular) partitions.

nodes.label: FloorSet-Lite
nodes.rationale: 1M-layout sub-dataset with rectangular-only partitions; sol is [w,h,x,y] plus a B*-tree representation. Used for the contest training/validation.

nodes.label: placement_constraints 5-tuple
nodes.rationale: Per-block constraint vector [fixed, preplaced, multi-instantiation(MIB), cluster, boundary]; boundary is a bitmask (L=1,R=2,T=4,B=8, corners combine).

nodes.label: FloorSet arXiv:2405.05480 (Mallappa 2024)
nodes.author: Uday Mallappa; Hesham Mostafa; Mikhail Galkin; Mariano Phielipp; Somdeb Majumdar

nodes.label: ICCAD 2026 Contest Problem C
nodes.rationale: The FloorSet Challenge: Data-Driven SoC Floorplanning; the team's contest track.

nodes.label: Intel Test Dataset (200 static circuits)
nodes.rationale: 100 Prime + 100 Lite static test circuits establishing a reproducible validation protocol; optimal metrics documented in intel_testsuite.md / intel_testsuite_lite.md.

nodes.label: FloorplanNet v1 (Unsupervised GCN)
nodes.rationale: 2-layer GCN trained with the differentiable contest cost for global placement; retired because the objective was wrong (learns to place, not reconstruct). Ceiling 3.3258 as a BL perm hint.

nodes.label: FloorplanNetV2 (Supervised MSE on fp_sol)
nodes.rationale: 4-layer residual GCN regressing absolute (x,y,w,h) from fp_sol; failed (downstream 4.2173, worse than no GNN) because absolute-position MSE on an ill-posed one-to-many map converges to blocks stacked in the middle.

nodes.label: FloorplanNetV3 (BL Ranking)
nodes.rationale: Shares the v2 encoder but predicts a structural BL ranking (pairwise BCE) to feed the BL packer; ranking signal exists but is weak (rank_acc ~0.58) and was abandoned after the oracle-perm ceiling.

nodes.label: Ill-posed One-to-Many Problem
nodes.rationale: Many legal layouts Y map to the same input X (connectivity/area/constraints), but training sees only one fp_sol; MSE averages over all Y and collapses. w/h is barely learnable (one aspect-ratio DoF), position is not.

nodes.label: Oracle-perm BL Packer Ceiling
nodes.rationale: Injecting oracle permutation + oracle shape shows the BL/SA pipeline caps at ~3.2-3.4 (perm-only 3.27, +1.8% over baseline; shape 3.42). The ceiling is the placer architecture, not ML input, so ML ranking training is not worth it.

nodes.label: iccad2026_evaluate.py
nodes.rationale: Evaluation framework: runs the optimizer on 100 cases, computes cost, provides auto-download dataloaders and the differentiable training loss; local RuntimeFactor forced to 1.0.

nodes.label: optimizer_template.py (B*-tree SA baseline)
nodes.rationale: Copy-and-replace baseline optimizer; participants implement solve() to place blocks.

nodes.label: training_example.py
nodes.rationale: Differentiable-training example demonstrating gradient flow through the proxy loss; currently the v3 ranking training script.

nodes.label: Contest Scoring Formula
nodes.rationale: Cost=(1+0.5(HPWL_gap+Area_gap))*exp(2*V_rel)*max(0.7,RuntimeFactor^0.3); gaps clamped to zero from below; infeasible=10.0; lower is better.

nodes.label: Hard Constraints
nodes.rationale: Violation => infeasible (10.0): no block overlaps, soft-block area within 1% of target, and dimension immutability for fixed-shape and preplaced blocks (preplaced also fixes x,y).

nodes.label: Soft Constraints
nodes.rationale: Penalized via exp(beta*V_rel): grouping (blocks abut into one connected component), MIB (identical dimensions), boundary (touch bounding-box edge/corner).

nodes.label: exp(n/12) Exponential Weighting
nodes.rationale: Total Score weights cases by e^(n/12) (n=block count 21-120); the smallest divisor giving every bucket non-zero weight while favoring large instances (n=116-120 bucket ~34%).

nodes.label: Runtime Normalization
nodes.rationale: Official RuntimeFactor is per-test-case cross-submission median; the local evaluator cannot replicate this (mixed-size median would distort) so it sets RuntimeFactor=1.0 (neutral) for every case.

nodes.label: solve() Optimizer Task
nodes.rationale: The method participants implement: given block_count, area_targets, b2b/p2b connectivity, pins_pos, constraints, return a list of (x,y,w,h) tuples minimizing wirelength and area.

nodes.label: tree_sol / fp_sol Training Labels
nodes.rationale: Training batch labels: fp_sol is the ground-truth (w,h,x,y) layout and tree_sol is its slicing/B*-tree representation; the reconstruction target.

nodes.label: compute_training_loss_differentiable
nodes.rationale: Differentiable proxy of the contest cost (HPWL gap, area gap, soft overlap and area-tolerance violations) enabling loss.backward(); omits RuntimeFactor and placement constraints.

nodes.label: get_training/validation_dataloader
nodes.rationale: Convenience functions in iccad2026_evaluate.py that auto-download FloorSet-Lite (1M training) and Lite-Test (100 validation) from Hugging Face as PyTorch DataLoaders.

nodes.label: Problem C Google Drive Submission
nodes.rationale: Problem C submits via the official Google Drive (not the VM); files go uncompressed into alpha_test/beta_test/final_test_submission folders; wrong filenames are non-resubmittable.

nodes.label: Competition VM Host (bare + offline)
nodes.rationale: Dev/test VM (host iccad010, 8 cores, ~251GB RAM) has g++ 8.5 + cmake but NO torch/numpy/shapely and NO network (pip cannot install, HuggingFace unreachable), so anything that must run there must be pure C++.

nodes.label: VM Cross-compiler Determinism Smoke Test
nodes.rationale: constructive.cpp compiled with VM g++ 8.5 -O3 -std=c++17 produced METRICS byte-identical to local msys g++ 13 on n=21/71/120 (5/53/114 ms), proving cross-compiler determinism: local tuning == scoring result.

nodes.label: Intel Test Suite (Prime, optimal metrics)
nodes.rationale: Table of 100 FloorSet-Prime test designs (intel_p1..p100, 21-120 partitions) with layout dims, area, nets, terminals, hard-constraint counts, and weighted HPWL metrics.

nodes.label: Intel Test Suite (Lite, optimal metrics)
nodes.rationale: Table of 100 FloorSet-Lite test designs (intel_lite21..120) with rectangular-partition layout dims, area, nets, terminals, hard-constraint counts, and weighted HPWL metrics.

nodes.label: Intel Test Layout Images (100 validation)
nodes.rationale: Directory of 100 validation test-case layout images, each annotated with placement constraints; optimal metrics documented in intel_testsuite.md.

nodes.label: torch (PyTorch)
nodes.rationale: Tensor/ML dependency (>=2.0.0) for dataset tensors, the differentiable loss and GNN models.

nodes.label: shapely
nodes.rationale: Geometry library (>=2.0.0) used for exact overlap/grouping scoring; the proxy vrel and final evaluation depend on it.

nodes.label: The FloorSet Challenge: Data-Driven SoC Floorplanning (ICCAD 2026 Contest v10)
nodes.author: Uday Mallappa; Sachin Bhat; Pei Chun Ch'ng; Somdeb Majumdar (Intel); Yuan Lu; Yusu Wang (UC San Diego)
nodes.rationale: Contest reframes SoC floorplanning as ML-guided optimization: shift from multi-day manual iterations to sub-minute automated cycles; performance-oriented, any algorithmic paradigm allowed.
nodes.norm_label: the floorset challenge: data-driven soc floorplanning (iccad 2026 contest v10)

nodes.label: Fixed-Outline Floorplanning
nodes.rationale: NP-complete combinatorial optimization: arrange blocks on a 2D canvas minimizing a multi-objective cost while satisfying all constraints.

nodes.label: SoC Floorplanning
nodes.rationale: Differs from bin packing: flexible shapes under area budgets, per-block placement constraints, connectivity to boundary terminals driving wirelength.

nodes.label: Soft Block (Module)
nodes.rationale: B = {b1..bk}; each block constrained by a predetermined area target ai; realized (w,h) may flex within 1% of ai.

nodes.label: Terminal (Fixed External Interface Point)
nodes.rationale: T = {t1..tr} predefined fixed points on the 2D plane; locations provided in input and remain fixed throughout the contest.

nodes.label: Inter-Module Connectivity (W_int)
nodes.rationale: Weighted adjacency matrix W_int in R^{k x k}; W_ij is the weight of the net connecting bi to bj; zero means no connection.

nodes.label: External Connectivity (W_ext)
nodes.rationale: Weighted adjacency matrix W_ext in R^{k x r}; weight of the net connecting block bi to terminal tj.

nodes.label: Objective / Cost Function (Eq. 2)
nodes.rationale: Cost = (1 + alpha*(HPWLgap + Areagap)) * exp(beta*Violations_rel) * max(0.7, RuntimeFactor^gamma) for feasible (capped at M-1e-6), else M. Constants alpha=0.5, beta=2.0, gamma=0.3; max(0.7,.) caps runtime benefit at 30%. Multi-objective: minimize area and wirelength while satisfying constraints.

nodes.label: Half-Perimeter Wirelength (HPWL)
nodes.rationale: Sums weighted Manhattan distances between centroids of connected blocks and terminals; centroid cx=x+w/2, cy=y+h/2.

nodes.label: Inter-Module HPWL (HPWL_int)
nodes.rationale: Sum over i, j>i of W_int_ij * (|cx_i - cx_j| + |cy_i - cy_j|); Manhattan distance between block centroids.

nodes.label: External HPWL (HPWL_ext)
nodes.rationale: Sum of W_ext_ij * Manhattan distance from block center to terminal (xtj, ytj).

nodes.label: HPWL Gap (HPWLgap)
nodes.rationale: (HPWLint + HPWLext - HPWLbaseline) / HPWLbaseline. 0 = matches baseline exactly; 0.15 = 15% worse than baseline.

nodes.label: Bounding-Box Area
nodes.rationale: Area_bbox = (xmax - xmin) * (ymax - ymin) over all block extents [xi, xi+wi] x [yi, yi+hi].

nodes.label: Bounding-Box Area Gap (Areagap)
nodes.rationale: (Area_bbox - Area_baseline) / Area_baseline. 0 = matches baseline; 0.05 = 5% more area than baseline.

nodes.label: Relative Violations (Violations_relative)
nodes.rationale: (Vgrouping + Vboundary + Vmib) / Nsoft, in [0,1]. Exponential penalty exp(2*V): 0.0->x1.00, 0.25->x1.65, 0.5->x2.72, 1.0->x7.39 (rapidly increasing).

nodes.label: Grouping Violation (Vgrouping)
nodes.rationale: Sum over groups of (cp - 1) where cp = connected components (blocks connected if they share an edge). Satisfied group cp=1; max violation |Gp|-1.

nodes.label: Boundary Violation (Vboundary)
nodes.rationale: Per-block: 1 if block does not touch its specified edge or corner of the bounding box, else 0.

nodes.label: Multi-Instantiation Violation (Vmib)
nodes.rationale: Sum over MIB groups of (sq - 1) where sq = distinct (w,h) pairs in group. Satisfied group sq=1; max violation |Mq|-1.

nodes.label: Soft Normalization Factor (Nsoft)
nodes.rationale: Nsoft = |Bboundary| + sum(|Gp|-1) + sum(|Mq|-1). Ensures Violations_relative in [0,1]. Fixed and preplaced excluded from soft constraints.

nodes.label: RuntimeFactor
nodes.rationale: RuntimeFactor = (Your Runtime / Median Runtime of All Submissions), applied as max(0.7, RF^0.3). Computed independently per test design using that case's median as sole reference. Slowness penalties are UNCAPPED; speed benefit capped at -30% (0.7 floor). Effects: 0.31->-30%, 0.5->-19%, 1.0(median) baseline, 2.0->+23%, 4.0->+51%.

nodes.label: Total Score
nodes.rationale: Weighted average of Cost[i] over 100 hidden test cases with weight omega_i = e^{ni/12} / Z, Z = sum_j e^{nj/12}. Lower is better; perfect baseline metrics at median runtime -> Total Score ~ 1.0.

nodes.label: Exponential Instance Weighting (e^{n/12})
nodes.rationale: Weight increases exponentially with block count so larger, more challenging instances (e.g. 120 blocks) contribute more heavily; penalizes methods that scale poorly and rewards ML that generalizes to large instances.

nodes.label: Grouping Constraint (Soft)
nodes.rationale: P groups of blocks that should be physically abutted (share a common edge segment of non-zero length, zero gap). Satisfied if all its blocks form a single connected component through shared edges.

nodes.label: Multi-Instantiation Blocks (MIB) Constraint (Soft)
nodes.rationale: Q groups where blocks should share identical dimensions (width and height); instances of the same master cell that must have uniform shape.

nodes.label: Boundary Constraint (Soft)
nodes.rationale: Blocks that should be placed so at least one edge touches the bounding-box boundary (edge constraint) or two edges touch a corner (corner constraint); specific edge/corner given per block in input.

nodes.label: Area Target / Dimensionality Constraint (Hard)
nodes.rationale: Soft blocks must satisfy |wi*hi - ai| / ai <= 0.01 (1% relative area tolerance); exceeding the tolerance is infeasible.

nodes.label: Overlap-Free Constraint (Hard)
nodes.rationale: Area(bi intersect bj) = 0 for any two distinct blocks; any intersection is infeasible. Blocks may share an edge (touch) without overlapping.

nodes.label: Fixed-Shape Immutability (Hard)
nodes.rationale: For b in Bfixed the solution (w,h) must exactly match input; target area ab is ignored. Infeasible if wb != wb_input or hb != hb_input. Previously soft, updated to hard in doc and evaluation code.

nodes.label: Preplaced Immutability (Hard)
nodes.rationale: For b in Bpreplaced both location AND dimensions must exactly match input; target area ab ignored. Infeasible if (xb,yb) or (wb,hb) differ from input. Previously soft, updated to hard.

nodes.label: Infeasible Penalty (M = 10)
nodes.rationale: Any hard-constraint violation gives fixed penalty M=10 for that test case: higher than any reasonable feasible solution, but not so extreme that a single failure dominates the total score.

nodes.label: Feasible Cost Cap (M - 1e-6)
nodes.rationale: Feasible costs capped at M - 1e-6 (<10) so any feasible solution, regardless of quality, always scores strictly better than an infeasible one. Feasible costs typically in [0.7, 7.4].

nodes.label: FloorSet Dataset
nodes.rationale: Provides millions of layout solutions where area and wirelength are demonstrably optimal and all placement constraints strictly satisfied; a definitive ground-truth reference enabling precise quantification of the optimality gap of any solver.

nodes.label: FloorSet-Lite Dataset
nodes.rationale: Curated subset with rectangular (hard) blocks and a fixed rectangular outline; streamlined high-fidelity environment lowering the entry barrier of full rectilinear/soft-block complexity for neural architectures. Optimal-by-construction layouts.

nodes.label: Training Split (1M samples, 21-120 blocks)
nodes.rationale: 1M samples with optimal solutions, sizes 21-120 blocks; for training ML models or analyzing structure. Access via get_training_dataloader() (Hugging Face).

nodes.label: Validation Split (100 samples)
nodes.rationale: 100 samples, one per size 21-120 blocks, accessible to contestants for validating generalizability. Access via get_validation_dataloader().

nodes.label: Test Split (100 hidden samples)
nodes.rationale: 100 samples, one per size 21-120 blocks, hidden from candidates; used for final submission evaluation.

nodes.label: Baseline Values (HPWLbaseline, Areabaseline)
nodes.rationale: Per-test-case optimal-by-construction HPWLbaseline and Areabaseline provided in the dataset; denominators for the gap-based normalizations (gap=0 means matching the baseline exactly).

nodes.label: ML-Guided Optimization
nodes.rationale: Hypothesized path to sub-minute automated cycles and foundation for agentic/conversational floorplanning; incentivized via runtime-in-score and exponential size weighting. Contest is performance-oriented, not method-restrictive.

nodes.label: Distributed Simulated Annealing (Proof-of-Concept)
nodes.rationale: Traditional heuristic (even with massive parallelism) struggles with FloorSet-Lite: for ~60 partitions, execution often exceeds 10 minutes without optimality, showing >=10% gap in wirelength or area.

nodes.label: Diffusion Model (Internal Counterpoint)
nodes.rationale: Organizers' internal diffusion-model experiment achieves high-fidelity solutions in sub-minute intervals, motivating data-driven approaches as a counterpoint to distributed SA.

nodes.label: Reverse-Engineering (Optimal-by-Construction) Methodology
nodes.rationale: Construction method that guarantees near-optimality, giving ground-truth (area/wirelength-optimal, constraint-satisfying) labels; the basis for FloorSet's definitive reference layouts.

nodes.label: Contest Repository (IntelLabs/FloorSet)
nodes.rationale: Provides PyTorch DataLoaders, score evaluators, infeasibility checks, plotting utilities and the required output/submission format; organizers strongly recommend verifying solutions with the provided evaluator before submission.

nodes.label: Anti-Reverse-Engineering Rule (Disqualification)
nodes.rationale: Submissions found reverse-engineering the dataset generator rather than developing genuine algorithmic solutions will be disqualified.
